$comment: Third-party versions OUTSIDE the npm lockfile (ADR-006, issue #1648).
npm and GitHub Actions are watched by Dependabot, and so are Terraform providers and the Gradle wrapper
(.github/dependabot.yml). This file covers what Dependabot cannot see or cannot decide: images we
BUILD from an upstream git tag (OZ Relayer, alto), images with a deliberate hold, toolchain lines
chosen in workflows, and the VM/Ansible pins. Container images ARE also watched by Dependabot's
docker / docker-compose ecosystems. They are listed here too, because coverage (V-04) and
exactness (V-05) are enforced by this file's gate, not by Dependabot.
status: track  = we intend to follow upstream; the weekly report shows how far behind we are.
status: hold   = deliberately behind. It needs hold.reason (why newer is worse FOR US), hold.ref
(the evidence), hold.reviewBy (no more than reviewWindowDays out), and hold.watch
(the upstream events that would lift it). An expired hold fails every pull request:
bump, or renew deliberately with fresh evidence.
locations[].contains must appear verbatim in that file and must contain `pinned` (V-03), so a bump
that forgets this registry fails in the same pull request.
exemptions are time-boxed exceptions to V-05 (floating tags). Same rule as holds: a reason, a
ref and an expiry. The list must only ever shrink.

exemptions.reason: First-party origin-lock image. Cloud Build pushes $SHORT_SHA alongside :latest, but the SHA actually running on the bundler VM is not recorded in the repo. Pinning a guessed SHA would be a fabricated fact; pin the deployed one once it has been read from Artifact Registry.

hold.reason: 1.5.0 introduced a receipt regression (upstream #817): a transient empty receipt from a load-balanced RPC finalizes a MINED tx as Failed and the confirmed webhook never fires. Our engine uses multi-endpoint public RPC failover, so we would hit it. 1.7.0's nonce-drift recovery jams when the drift region is full (#843). The cap-bound stuck lane (#808) affects 1.4.0 through 1.8.0 alike, so bumping does not fix it; it is mitigated by the probe and the runbook instead. NOTE: the production compose tag is `multichain-v1.5.0`, whose base engine version is not recorded in-repo; verifying it is #1650.

pins.notes: Value path (sponsored UserOps). A bump soaks on the e2e passkey stack first, then on one chain's VM. Respect G-11: at most one alto per (chain, executor EOA).
One Node line across every image and CI. Node 22 reaches EOL 2027-04-30, so the 24 migration must be planned by 2027-01-30 (ADR-006: 90 days ahead).

upstream.why: setup-node resolves the newest 22.x at run time; the line, not the patch, is the decision. Its EOL is what the report watches.

pins.notes: Stable line. Moved off `nginx:alpine` (SPA, floating mainline) and `1.27-alpine` (origin lock, EOL 2025-06-24) on 2026-10-09.
Holds the relay engine's nonce lanes (ephemeral). 8.x is a major and a license change (AGPL/RSAL/SSPL tri-license); it is a separate decision, not a routine bump.
Plan and apply must use the SAME version (apply executes the reviewed plan). Bump all three together.
Tracks what the nodes already run (see the comment at the pin). Converge restarts containers; bump in a maintenance window.

upstream.why: A language line is chosen, not followed; its EOL is the signal. Moved off 3.10 (EOL 2026-10-01) on 2026-10-09.
Held on an EOL line on purpose; see hold. The report shows the EOL.

hold.reason: Manticore is unmaintained upstream (Trail of Bits archived it) and its native extras plus the protobuf<=3.20.3 pin do not install on newer Pythons. Moving the line means replacing the tool, not bumping it, so it is decided together with the torture-test toolchain review.

upstream.why: A language line is chosen, not followed; its EOL is the signal. Medusa itself is installed @latest, which is the floating pin the follow-up removes.
capacitor-android compiles at Java 21 (CLAUDE.md, spec 102). The line follows Capacitor, not Java releases.
